purpose: Prove Multi team capability actually runs a collaboration loop with a real model. Not a Terminal-Bench score, and not a claim that Multi is better on hard work.

scope_limits.notes: The fixture states the finding outright and the instruction prescribes which tools to call in which order, so gate 1 answers 'does the team machinery actually fire end to end under a real model', not 'does Multi help on a task with real analysis'. Deliberate: decision 010 froze this carrier because a single-operator task lets the model finish alone and never touch a team tool, which would fail gate 1 for task difficulty rather than for a product defect. The WBS phrase 'full collaboration semantics on a real task' is only satisfied by gate 1 and gate 2 read together: gate 1 supplies the collaboration evidence, gate 2 supplies the real tasks. Neither gate alone may be quoted as satisfying it.
scope_limits.gate2_order_bias: base_order runs Codex before Multi on every task, so Multi inherits a warmed image. That bias favours Multi, and gate 2 only calls degradation when Codex completes and Multi does not, so it makes the degradation verdict more conservative rather than fabricating one. It does weaken a 'no degradation observed' reading.
scope_limits.runtime_bundle: runtime-v4 retains a plaintext code-mode cell result only at a terminal response boundary after a supported non-team nested dispatch completed. Team-state and evidence-read-only cells do not recursively create Facts. Evidence produced by runtime-v1/v2/v3 belongs to earlier workflow contracts and must not be replayed against this lock.

finding_line: M5-COLLAB-FINDING: orders.legacy_total is dropped by migration 0042

evidence_source.wait_signal: Wait completed: the team world state changed. The current active view is in this request.
evidence_source.notes: Under tool_mode=code_mode_only the model emits one custom_tool_call named `exec` carrying JavaScript, and every team tool is called from inside that script. The Responses wire therefore carries only what the script printed -- text the model authored about its own tool calls -- so it cannot be the judge's evidence. The judge instead reads the frozen binary's rollout-trace bundle, whose ToolCallStarted/ToolCallEnded pairs are written by the Rust dispatch path and carry the registry's own tool name, namespace, arguments and handler return value. The Responses capture is still required and is used to bind: every dispatch in the judged trace must belong to a code cell whose model_visible_call_id appears as a captured custom_tool_call and whose recorded source_js is contained in that call's input, so a bundle from another run cannot be replayed as evidence; any Direct model dispatch fails the run closed. Both the team world-state tools and the multi-agent v2 tools are registered through the same namespace override, so the registry reports them under `collaboration` and code mode binds them as `collaboration__<name>`. A supported non-team result nested in a cell is folded into the retained outer exec result; runtime-v4 accepts that outer result as evidence only when the nested result completed before the terminal response boundary and every retained content item is plaintext input_text. Yielded responses, team-state or evidence-read-only cells, mixed media, encrypted bodies, unavailable cells, and unbound output items are rejected whole. The offline rehearsal uses this same code-mode shell shape rather than injecting a direct shell call. Its required dump and log each request limit=3 and must continue through at least two completed pages to a null cursor or offset, so collector continuation is exercised rather than inferred. Only a completed required team_inspect dispatch yields dump/log rows. Root wake requires a completed wait_agent on the manifest's exact root thread returning TeamActivity; a member wait or log-only signal is insufficient. TEAM_REPORT is never collaboration evidence.

collaboration_predicates.description: Root spawned exactly one member. Dump has a non-root participant.
The selected Event has at least one Root Version and two member Versions.
Those Versions on the same Event were written by at least two distinct authors, including the member.
After Root's own Version completes, the manifest Root thread completes a route assignment on that Event targeting the same member.

After Root published and routed the Event, the same member completed team_evidence on its first Version's exact exec Fact before appending a distinct second Version; the available, successful, untruncated result is produced by that member and its non-empty observation contains the frozen finding.
After the distinct second member Version, the manifest Root thread completed team_update and the inspect log records a later set_root_state revision resolving that exact member-authored Version.

The manifest Root thread was already waiting when the first member publish started; that publish completed before the wait returned TeamActivity, and the exact inspect-log publish revision records member_publish waking the manifest Root before Root's own publish.

attempts.semantics: Each attempt is an independent run with its own versioned run id and immutable evidence. A pass stops the gate. An evidence or product failure continues to the next attempt and keeps its original classification. A budget or authorization stop ends the gate immediately. Resume skips archived attempts, safely reclaims only a zero-request pristine ledger run with no capture artifacts, records a pristine run with exact pre-request owned artifacts exactly once as abandoned infra before continuing, and does the same for a requested but unarchived retryable-infra run. Unsafe artifacts, Harbor-started state, Docker residue, unknown stops, and identity or ordering conflicts fail closed.
